records.title: Mst. Farzana Bibi v. C.C.P.O. Lahore (Crl. Misc. 36448/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: The Supreme Court decision ending the policy of appointing children of deceased or retired civil servants (omission of Rule 17-A, Punjab Civil Servants (Appointment & Conditions of Service) Rules 1974) applies prospectively from the date of that decision. Cases where the parent died or retired on medical grounds before then remain covered. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 389; Muhammad Zaman v. Government of the Punjab (WP 12771-24).
records.title: Muhammad Zaman v. Government of the Punjab (WP 12771-24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: After an FIR is cancelled, the police may reinvestigate the case, but only with the permission of the Magistrate concerned. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 398, 2024 MLD 1796; Muhammad Aslam Khan v. Judicial Magistrate Ferozewala (Crl. Proceedings 9158/24).
records.title: Muhammad Aslam Khan v. Judicial Magistrate Ferozewala (Crl. Proceedings 9158/24)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.topic: Family Pension: Unmarried Daughter; Succession Certificate
records.text: Under the pension rules as amended in 1999, the eldest unmarried daughter of a deceased government servant draws her share of family pension until marriage, after which it passes to the next unmarried daughter. Proceedings for a succession certificate under the Succession Act 1925 are summary, and a second application was wrongly held barred by Order II Rule 2 CPC. Ref: 2025 SCMR 579, PLJ 2025 SC 183; Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020).
records.title: Mst. Anita Anam v. General Public (C.P.L.A. 256-Q/2020)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Remedy against Revisional Decree on Rejection of Plaint
records.text: Explains the remedy available where a District Court, in revisional jurisdiction, passes a decree on rejection of a plaint, and the need for a real link between an alleged procedural irregularity and the substantive rights of the parties. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 24, PLJ 2025 SC 207; Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A. 81-P/2019).
records.title: Misree Khan v. Abdul Ghafoor (C.P.L.A. 81-P/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Whether time is of the essence depends on the wording of the agreement and the intention of the parties, and is a question of fact. Where time is not of the essence, failure to perform by the date fixed does not make the agreement voidable; the promisee is left to compensation. Ref: 2025 SCMR 495, PLJ 2025 SC 188; Zeeshan Pervez v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022).
records.title: Zeeshan Pervez v. Muhammad Nasir (C.P.L.A. 812-K/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Motive is a double-edged weapon that may explain either real or false implication; an accused cannot be held guilty on the basis of motive alone. The judgment also sets out the medical differences between hanging and strangulation. Ref: 2024 SCMR 1507, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 73; Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa v. The State.
records.title: Muhammad Ijaz alias Billa v. The State

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.text: S. 34 PPC does not require each accused to act with his own hand; a prearranged plan and participation in furtherance of the common intention suffice. S. 109 PPC: an abettor is punishable as for the offence abetted where it is committed in consequence of the abetment. Honour killing (karo-kari) is murder simpliciter, not permitted by law or religion, and an offence committed on the pretext of honour falls within "fasad-fil-arz" under s. 299(ee) PPC. The judgment also explains the term "sui juris". Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 87; Muhammad Ali Mahar v. The State (Crl. P. 201-K of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Mahar v. The State (Crl. P. 201-K of 2023)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: The power to suspend sentence under s. 426 CrPC is narrower than the power to grant bail under ss. 497 and 498 CrPC. A convict who absconds after suspension of sentence must be taken into custody before any application by him (including for correction under s. 369 or s. 561-A CrPC) is entertained. Application dismissed. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 661.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO: Declaring Own Witness Hostile
records.text: Permission to cross-examine one's own witness under Art. 150 QSO is in the discretion of the court and is given only where the witness turns against the party calling him. Refusal to declare defence witnesses hostile upheld in revision under ss. 435 and 439 CrPC. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 644.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Quashing of FIR: Dishonoured Cheques (s. 489-F PPC)
records.text: Several post-dated cheques issued for a sale of tractors were dishonoured on different dates and separate FIRs were registered. The plea of double jeopardy failed because each cheque was a separate transaction; dismissal of the s. 249-A CrPC application and of the quashing petition upheld. Charges for cheques dishonoured within twelve months may be joined under s. 234 CrPC. Recording the complainant's statement at his residence through a commission was upheld. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 648.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 75 PPC: Enhanced Punishment for Previous Conviction
records.text: S. 75 PPC allows enhanced punishment where the accused has a previous conviction for an offence under Chapter XII or XVII PPC. Under s. 221(7) CrPC the fact, date and place of the previous conviction must be stated in the charge, and may be added before sentence; the prosecution must prove it. The investigating officer must trace and produce the record of previous convictions. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 786.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: A wife divorced by triple talaq pronounced at one sitting inherits from her husband if he dies before her iddat expires. Ref: Aziz Ahmad v. Mst. Musarat (C.P.L.A. 181/2023, decided 09.04.2025); Justice Shakeel Ahmad.
records.title: Aziz Ahmad v. Mst. Musarat (C.P.L.A. 181/2023, decided 09.04.2025)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A witness to a document who, when deposing, does not speak to its contents or does not verify his signature or thumb impression on it cannot be treated as an attesting witness. The judgment also explains what exhibiting a document by the court means. Ref: PLD 2018 Lah 132.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Vakalatnama: No Implied Power to Compromise
records.text: A power of attorney or vakalatnama does not impliedly authorise counsel to compromise, withdraw the suit or concede a decree; such powers must be specifically conferred. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 414; Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (WP 3631-15).
records.title: Falak Sher v. Hashmat Bibi (WP 3631-15)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Art. 40 QSO: Discovery; Last Seen Evidence
records.text: Sets out seven essentials of Art. 40 QSO: lawful police custody in that case at the time of disclosure; specific information distinctly relating to the fact discovered; a tangible discovery of a fact previously unknown to the police; a direct causal link between disclosure and discovery; admissibility of only the part relating distinctly to the discovery; a genuine recovery proved through credible, preferably independent, witnesses; and corroboration, since a discovery alone cannot sustain a conviction. Also discusses last seen evidence. Directions issued for circulation of the judgment. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 36; Zunair Younas v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 532/2018, decided 22.04.2025); Justice Salahuddin Panhwar.
records.title: Zunair Younas v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 532/2018, decided 22.04.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: If eye-witnesses are disbelieved against co-accused given effective roles, they cannot be believed against another accused with a similar role without independent corroboration. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 383; Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal 198/2023).
records.title: Ameeruddin v. The State (Criminal Appeal 198/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Delay may be condoned only on a reasonable explanation of each day's delay. An appeal filed about two years late, after an earlier appeal was dismissed by the High Court for lack of pecuniary jurisdiction, was not saved; ss. 5 and 14 Limitation Act 1908 apply only where the party acted with due diligence. Government bodies get no special treatment. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 371.

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: S. 22(3) Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009: Deposit of Rent
records.text: S. 22(3) Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 is directory. A party cannot be compelled to deposit rent in court until the relationship of landlord and tenant is established. Ref: 2025 LHC 2894; Shabana Parveen v. Malik Mohsin Hassan Rasheed (WP 45912/22, decided 06.05.2025); Justice Malik Waqar Haider Awan.
records.title: Shabana Parveen v. Malik Mohsin Hassan Rasheed (WP 45912/22, decided 06.05.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Art. 150 QSO and S. 342 CrPC in Narcotics Trial
records.text: Where a prosecution witness in a narcotics case deposes against the prosecution on some points and is neither re-examined nor cross-examined on them under Art. 150 QSO, those points stand unrebutted. A piece of evidence not put to the accused in his statement under s. 342 CrPC cannot be used against him (1500 grams charas case). Ref: 2025 YLR 867, PLJ 2025 CrC 35; Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 40132/23).
records.title: Mst. Shahidah Bibi v. The State (Crl. Appeal 40132/23)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.text: S. 506 PPC has no part "(ii)" or "(B)". Its latter part (threat to cause death, grievous hurt and the like, punishable up to seven years) is a continuation of the first part and is not to be read as a separate offence; the practice of citing "506(ii)" or "506-B" is a misquotation that must stop. Ref: 2025 MLD 714; Habib ur Rehman v. The State (Crl. Misc. 56879-B/2024).
records.title: Habib ur Rehman v. The State (Crl. Misc. 56879-B/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: The onset and duration of rigor mortis vary with body condition, age, muscle mass, temperature, illness and body fat, which must be kept in view when relying on it to fix the time of death. Ref: 2025 YLR 1001; The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Murder Reference 300-19).
records.title: The State v. Munir Hussain Shah (Murder Reference 300-19)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Fire Shots from Back: Minor Discrepancy
records.text: A deceased under fire is not static and may receive shots from behind; an eye-witness is not expected to give the exact location and direction of each shot. Such discrepancies do not discredit the ocular account. Ref: 2025 SCMR 935; Akbar Saeed v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1366/2018).
records.title: Akbar Saeed v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1366/2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Medico-Ocular Conflict on Number of Injuries
records.text: A conflict between the ocular and medical evidence about the number of injuries suffered by the deceased is fatal to the prosecution case. Ref: 2025 SCMR 944; Chetan v. The State (Crl.A. 94/2023).
records.title: Chetan v. The State (Crl.A. 94/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Benefit of doubt does not need many circumstances; a single circumstance creating reasonable doubt in a prudent mind entitles the accused to it as of right, and every doubt in the prosecution case goes to the accused. Ref: 2025 SCMR 810, 2025 SCMR 880.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: The presumption of genuineness of a document more than 30 years old (Art. 100 QSO) is rebuttable and arises only where the document comes from proper custody and is unsuspicious. A dower deed produced by its scriber, who had no proper custody of it, did not attract the presumption. Ref: 2025 SCMR 841; Muhammad Israr v. Jehanzeb (C.A. 156-P/2013).
records.title: Muhammad Israr v. Jehanzeb (C.A. 156-P/2013)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: The first question for eye-witnesses is whether they saw the occurrence and could identify the assailants. Abscondence is only corroborative, cannot be read in isolation and cannot cure defects in the prosecution case. Ref: 2025 SCMR 888; Muhammad Masood alias Mithu v. The State (J.P. 441/2017).
records.title: Muhammad Masood alias Mithu v. The State (J.P. 441/2017)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Benefit of doubt must rest on a reasonable doubt, not on minor discrepancies. If trivial contradictions were given weight there would hardly be any conviction; they cannot be the sole ground for acquittal. Ref: 2025 SCMR 894; Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A. 229/2021).
records.title: Sher Afzal v. The State (Crl.A. 229/2021)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Safe Custody and Transmission of Case Property
records.text: In narcotics cases the prosecution must prove safe custody and transmission of the case property through documentary evidence (malkhana register, road certificates). The bare oral statement of the moharrir or malkhana incharge is not enough. Investigating agencies must investigate on true lines in the spirit of the CNSA 1997. Ref: 2025 SCMR 923; Jeehand v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1187/2021).
records.title: Jeehand v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1187/2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Abscondence by itself is no ground to refuse bail if the accused is otherwise entitled to it on merits. Authorities listed: 2025 SCMR 318, 2024 SCMR 464, 2024 SCMR 1716, 2023 SCMR 1948, 2023 SCMR 1898, 2023 SCMR 2122, 2023 SCMR 172, 2022 SCMR 547, 2021 SCMR 1295, 2020 SCMR 547. Ref: 2025 SCMR 318, 2024 SCMR 464, 2024 SCMR 1716, 2023 SCMR 1948 and others.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Pre-Arrest Bail: Merits May Be Considered
records.text: While deciding pre-arrest bail the court may touch upon the merits of the case. Authorities listed: 2023 SCMR 2181, 884, 1152, 1773, 330, 1729, 1712, 581, 1898; 2022 SCMR 547; 2021 SCMR 1295; 2020 SCMR 956. Ref: 2023 SCMR 2181, 2023 SCMR 884, 2023 SCMR 1152, 2023 SCMR 1773 and others.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Change of Company Name in Record of Rights
records.text: An application to record a change in the name of a company in the record of rights is not a sale and does not attract s. 42 Punjab Land Revenue Act as a transfer. The revenue authorities' order treating it as a sale was set aside. Ref: 2025 CLC 760; Messrs Popular Sugar Mills Ltd v. District Collector, Sargodha (WP 40356 of 2019).
records.title: Messrs Popular Sugar Mills Ltd v. District Collector, Sargodha (WP 40356 of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Additional Evidence to Be Decided First
records.text: An application for additional evidence under O. XLI R. 27 CPC pending in appeal must be decided before the appeal is decided on merits. Deciding the appeal without first resolving it is a procedural irregularity that vitiates the judgment. Ref: 2025 CLC 727; Muhammad Iqbal Gill v. Nasir Abbas (C.R. 6830 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal Gill v. Nasir Abbas (C.R. 6830 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Under Art. 113 Limitation Act 1908, a suit for specific performance must be filed within three years of the date fixed for performance or, if none is fixed, from when the plaintiff has notice of refusal. A date having been fixed in the agreement, the suit filed beyond three years was time-barred; concurrent dismissal upheld. Ref: 2025 CLC 638; Muhammad Alam v. Darbari Khan (C.R. 40284 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Alam v. Darbari Khan (C.R. 40284 of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: The second marriage of the mother is not by itself a bar to her custody of the child if she is otherwise suitable; the welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration. Father's petition dismissed. Ref: 2025 MLD 773; Amjad Ali v. Additional District Judge, Pattoki (WP 76865).
records.title: Amjad Ali v. Additional District Judge, Pattoki (WP 76865)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: A civil revision filed 122 days after the decision, against the 90 days allowed by Art. 162-A Limitation Act, was time-barred. Unsupported claims of illness, old age or ignorance of office procedure do not justify condonation; the decision had become a past and closed transaction. Ref: 2025 MLD 749, PLJ 2025 Civil Note 57; Muhammad Anwar v. Shahadat Ali (C.R. 61696 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Anwar v. Shahadat Ali (C.R. 61696 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Where a Muslim dies without residuaries, the surplus returns to the sharers under the doctrine of return (radd). On the facts, the sons of the paternal uncle took as residuaries after the sharers, and the revenue hierarchy rightly gave them their shares. Ref: 2025 MLD 662; Kaniz Haider v. Khaliq Dad (WPs 80553, 80520, 80539 & 80547 of 2023).
records.title: Kaniz Haider v. Khaliq Dad (WPs 80553, 80520, 80539 & 80547 of 2023)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A CDR must bear the seal, signature or authentication letter of the telecom company that issued it. A bare, unsigned CDR cannot be considered or relied upon at trial. Ref: Khair Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P. 132 of 2018, decided 30.04.2025).
records.title: Khair Muhammad v. The State (Crl.P. 132 of 2018, decided 30.04.2025)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Summoning CDR of Raiding Party
records.text: S. 94 CrPC places no stage limit on the court's power to order production of a document. During a narcotics trial the accused may apply for the call data record of the raiding police officials, notwithstanding that s. 265-F(7) CrPC gives a similar opportunity at the defence stage. Ref: Muhammad Ikram v. The State (Criminal Appeal 1-Q/2025, decided 20.05.2025); Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar; Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim; Justice Ali Baqar Najafi.
records.title: Muhammad Ikram v. The State (Criminal Appeal 1-Q/2025, decided 20.05.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Mere abscondence is not proof of guilt. A post-mortem conducted 21 hours after the occurrence, with the doctor giving the same interval between death and post-mortem, contradicted the ocular account. Ref: 2025 MLD 982; Muhammad Shahbaz Honey v. The State (Crl. Appeal 15995/20).
records.title: Muhammad Shahbaz Honey v. The State (Crl. Appeal 15995/20)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Prior Unregistered vs Subsequent Registered Document
records.text: Considers (i) whether courts may prefer a prior unregistered document over a later registered document for the same immovable property, and (ii) whether findings may rest on facts wrongly asserted in the plaint and inconsistent with the evidence when the documents show otherwise. Ref: 2025 MLD 847; Muhammad Ramzan v. Haleema Bibi (Civil Revision 346-18).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. Haleema Bibi (Civil Revision 346-18)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Forensic Report: Human Blood without Grouping
records.text: A forensic report showing only human blood on the weapon, without determining its group or matching it with the blood of the deceased, has no evidentiary value. Ref: 2025 MLD 818, PLJ 2025 CrC 326; Ali Akbar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 31052/23).
records.title: Ali Akbar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 31052/23)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Where the defence takes a specific plea and the prosecution has proved its case, the trend of cross-examination of prosecution witnesses may also be considered in assessing the case. On the facts, the evidence showed that only the inmates of the house were present at the time of the incident. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 386; Shafqat Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 10245/22).
records.title: Shafqat Ali v. The State (Jail Appeal 10245/22)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Where the accused was related to and known to the complainant and injured but was not named in the FIR or in the injured's statement, his later nomination through supplementary statements needs verification at trial. Case of further inquiry; bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 414; Muhammad Kashif Shehzad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 77329/24).
records.title: Muhammad Kashif Shehzad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 77329/24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Where the medical evidence wholly contradicts the ocular account, the prosecution story becomes improbable and suggests that the true facts have been suppressed or are unknown to the prosecution. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 432; M. Ali Yasir v. The State (Crl. Appeal 9553/21).
records.title: M. Ali Yasir v. The State (Crl. Appeal 9553/21)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Offence Committed Abroad by Pakistani Citizen
records.text: Under s. 3 PPC and ss. 188 and 403 CrPC, a Pakistani who commits abroad an act that is an offence under the PPC may be tried in Pakistan as if it were committed here; s. 188 CrPC does not bar registration of an FIR under s. 154 CrPC. The protection of s. 403 CrPC is available only after a trial by a competent court ending in conviction or acquittal. On the facts, ingredients of criminal breach of trust (s. 405 PPC) by an employee were made out. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 442; Muhammad Irshad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 7151-B/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 7151-B/2025)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Fraud or forgery need not be reported only by the person directly affected; it is a crime against the public and may be reported by anyone. Forgery of a sale deed (a valuable security) attracts s. 467 PPC, punishable with imprisonment for life, so the offence falls within the prohibitory clause of s. 497 CrPC. The court may itself consider the applicable offence at the bail stage even if the investigating officer did not add it. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 448; Riaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 8612-B/2025).
records.title: Riaz Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 8612-B/2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 173 CrPC: Defective Investigation vs Defective Report
records.text: Distinguishes a "defective investigation report" from a "defective investigation" and issues directions to investigating officers, prosecutors, sessions judges, magistrates and jail superintendents for timely submission of reports under s. 173 CrPC, following Hakeem Mumtaz and the DDJ instructions of 26.07.2021. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 453; Rahat Abbas v. The State (Crl. Misc. 1979-B-24).
records.title: Rahat Abbas v. The State (Crl. Misc. 1979-B-24)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Conflict between Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.text: Eye-witnesses put the occurrence at 7.00 a.m. but the doctor's estimate of time between death and post-mortem (9 to 10 hours, at 10.00 a.m.) placed it around midnight to 1.00 a.m. The medical evidence contradicted the ocular account. Ref: PLJ 2025 SC CrC 108; Muhammad Ashraf v. The State (Crl. A. 188 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. The State (Crl. A. 188 of 2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Recovery is only corroborative; once the ocular account is disbelieved for conflict with the medical evidence, a recovery standing alone has no independent value. A witness disbelieved against his own assailant is of little help in sustaining the rest of the case. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 180.

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Acquitted Case Not to Be Shown
records.text: Once a person is acquitted and the acquittal is final, he is absolved in law, and continuing to show the FIR in a police character certificate violates his dignity under Art. 14 of the Constitution. Petitioner held entitled to a character certificate reflecting the acquittal and no subsisting criminal liability. Ref: 2025 LHC 5162; Abdul Rehman Faryad v. Government of the Punjab (WP 40844 of 2025, decided 18.07.2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman Faryad v. Government of the Punjab (WP 40844 of 2025, decided 18.07.2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.text: Where the tenant did not dispute the rate of rent, the Rent Tribunal rightly directed deposit of tentative rent by the 10th of each month, subject to adjustment. Default in paying tentative rent justified the ejectment order under s. 24 Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009. Ref: PLD 2023 Lah 47.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A photocopy of a document can be read only as secondary evidence. Without proof of loss of the original, a photocopy is inadmissible even if exhibited without objection. Ref: 2025 MLD 1165.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Statement before Court: Enforceability in Execution
records.text: A statement or undertaking made before the court, on which the suit was disposed of, is enforceable by the executing court. On the facts, the defendant's undertaking about arranging water drainage at shared cost was enforced and his application accepted. Ref: 2025 MLD 1144.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: The presumption of truth attached to a registered nikahnama is rebuttable. A nikahnama shown as registered after the husband's death, without the first and fourth copies being produced, did not prove the marriage for a dower claim against his heirs. The presumption of truth attaches only to the first and fourth parts of the nikahnama, which remain in official custody. Ref: 2025 MLD 1102, PLJ 2024 Civil Note 218.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Blackening and Burning: Distance of Fire
records.text: Blackening and burning around a firearm wound appear only when the shot is fired from a few inches. A shot fired from about five feet cannot cause burning. Ref: 2025 MLD 1085.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.text: Art. 164 QSO permits evidence from modern devices. Although cameras were available, the complainant and investigating officer did not record the recovery of 1230 grams of heroin; the best evidence was withheld. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 170.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: A DNA report is not primary evidence and can only corroborate. Last seen evidence is the weakest kind of evidence unless corroborated. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 172.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Bail: Female Accused, Recovery Not Recorded
records.text: Recovery of 1600 grams of charas was not video-recorded and the conduct of the police showed bias, raising doubt about the petitioner's involvement. Being a woman she fell under the first proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC, investigation was complete, and the case was one of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC. Bail allowed. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 174.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 341 CrPC: Accused Unable to Understand Proceedings
records.text: If the judge doubts that the accused can understand the proceedings, the procedure in s. 341 CrPC must be followed. If the trial ends in conviction of an accused who cannot understand, the trial court must not pass sentence but forward the proceedings to the High Court. On the facts, a deaf and mute accused found not insane by a medical board, the trial court made the reference without properly complying with s. 341; matter remanded. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 657, PLJ 2025 CrC 550; The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi (Reference under s. 341 CrPC 69061/20).
records.title: The State v. Saqib Hussain Qureshi (Reference under s. 341 CrPC 69061/20)

records.subject: General Notes
records.text: The right to information under Art. 19-A of the Constitution and the Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act 2013 is not absolute. Personal information protected by the privacy exception in s. 13(1)(b) of the Act may be withheld. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 649; Shahbaz Akmal Jandran v. Province of Punjab (WP 22041/25).
records.title: Shahbaz Akmal Jandran v. Province of Punjab (WP 22041/25)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.text: The testimony of a victim with a cognitive or intellectual disability must not be rejected outright. Courts, police and prosecutors must provide procedural accommodations. On the facts, the trial court held a voir dire and found the deaf and mute victim incompetent, but failed to explore alternative means of recording her evidence; direction to summon a forensic psychologist or psychiatrist. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 641; Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Crl. Appeal 692/2022) with Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 704-J/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Ramzan v. The State (Crl. Appeal 692/2022) with Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 704-J/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: S. 152 CPC allows correction of clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgments and decrees, and s. 151 CPC preserves inherent powers to secure the ends of justice. A deliberate or intentional decision cannot be altered under these sections; it can be corrected only in review, appeal or revision. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 682, PLJ 2025 Lah 223; Muhammad Hussain v. Ali Muhammad (Civil Revision 1499 of 2012).
records.title: Muhammad Hussain v. Ali Muhammad (Civil Revision 1499 of 2012)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XLI R. 27 CPC: Timing of Decision on Additional Evidence
records.text: No rule requires an application for additional evidence to be decided by a separate order before the appeal. Whether to decide it first or together with the appeal depends on the facts; the aim is a complete and satisfactory judgment. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 704; Mushtaq Ahmad v. Saiqa Chaudhary (C.R. 1077-24).
records.title: Mushtaq Ahmad v. Saiqa Chaudhary (C.R. 1077-24)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Custody: Remarriage of Mother; Absent Father
records.text: A father living abroad who has never met his daughter cannot claim custody merely as natural guardian because the mother has remarried. Remarriage of the mother does not by itself disqualify her; the court weighs both parents' circumstances and the minor's welfare and attachment. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 541, PLJ 2025 SC 307; Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano (C.P.L.A. 3920/2024).
records.title: Asjad Ullah v. Mst. Aisa Bano (C.P.L.A. 3920/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 100 CPC: Second Appeal; Specific Performance Discretionary
records.text: Second appeal under s. 100 CPC lies only on the limited grounds stated in the section. Specific performance is a discretionary, equitable relief; on the facts (four plots, substantial consideration unpaid, part paid to a deceased party), the claim of adjustment towards the plots was rejected. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 567; Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Aijaz (C.A. 99-K/2022).
records.title: Muhammad Azam v. Muhammad Aijaz (C.A. 99-K/2022)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: A married daughter remains a child of her deceased parent and is equally entitled to appointment under the deceased-employee rule (Rule 10(4)); her exclusion on marriage is discriminatory. An executive clarification cannot override statutory rules. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 529; Zahida Parveen v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.P.L.A. 566-P/2024).
records.title: Zahida Parveen v. Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (C.P.L.A. 566-P/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Offence Omitted or Added after Bail
records.text: If an offence is inadvertently left out of a bail petition, or added after bail is granted, and the jail superintendent will not release the accused, the accused may apply to the court concerned, because bail is granted in the case and not for a particular offence. Ref: 2020 YLR 356, 2004 PCrLJ 399, 2018 PCrLJ 837.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Unexplained delay in reporting makes the FIR an unreliable foundation for the prosecution case. A witness who makes dishonest improvements, or denies admitted facts, cannot be relied on. Prosecution failed to prove its case; appellant acquitted. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 645; Karamat Ali v. The State (Crl. A. 5394 & M.R. 12 of 2022).
records.title: Karamat Ali v. The State (Crl. A. 5394 & M.R. 12 of 2022)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A scribe is a competent witness of a document only if he also signed it as an attesting witness. While attesting witnesses are alive and available, a document whose execution is denied cannot be used without calling them; otherwise it is inadmissible. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 894; Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed (C.R. 441-D of 2018).
records.title: Shabbir Hussain v. Muhammad Shabbir Naveed (C.R. 441-D of 2018)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Sole Testimony of Prosecutrix; S. 540 CrPC
records.text: The rule that the sole testimony of the prosecutrix may be accepted is not absolute. Under s. 540 CrPC the court must summon a witness whose evidence is essential to a just decision; the investigating officer is such a witness, and the court's failure to summon him (even by coercive process) prejudiced the appellants. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC Note 195; Zia alias Ziai v. The State (Crl. A. 81 & 85 of 2012).
records.title: Zia alias Ziai v. The State (Crl. A. 81 & 85 of 2012)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cross-Examination on Same Day; Minor Contradictions
records.text: Once examination-in-chief is over, cross-examination should be completed the same day or, if time runs out, the next day. Minor contradictions from fading memory do not discredit a truthful witness. An accused who sets up a specific defence must show that the preponderance of probability supports it. Ref: PLJ 2025 CrC 686; Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State (Crl. A. 83064 of 2023; Crl. Rev. 2545 of 2024).
records.title: Muhammad Amir alias Aneel v. The State (Crl. A. 83064 of 2023; Crl. Rev. 2545 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Where no objection was taken to the non-framing of an issue at trial or in appeal, and the parties knew the dispute and led evidence on it, the omission is inconsequential. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 905; Muhammad Irshad v. Muhammad Ramzan (R.F.A. 206 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Irshad v. Muhammad Ramzan (R.F.A. 206 of 2023)

records.subject: General Notes
records.text: A judgment is authority only for the issues it decides and cannot be generalised to matters outside its scope. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 572.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Disputed documents tendered through the statement of counsel cannot be considered, since the other side is denied the chance to test them in cross-examination. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 661.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Mutation Not an Instrument (Art. 91); Documents through Counsel
records.text: A mutation is not an "instrument" for the purposes of Art. 91 Limitation Act 1908. Documents tendered through counsel's statement after evidence and cross-examination have closed are inadmissible. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 724, PLJ 2025 Lah 699; Muhammad Manzoor v. Muhammad Shafi (Civil Revision 3483-14).
records.title: Muhammad Manzoor v. Muhammad Shafi (Civil Revision 3483-14)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Criminal Breach of Trust in Business Dealings
records.text: Criminal breach of trust needs entrustment of property (amanat) and its dishonest misappropriation or conversion. The Supreme Court disapproved the routine registration of s. 406 PPC FIRs in money and business disputes, which are civil in nature, and directed that the judgment be circulated for compliance. Offence not within the prohibitory clause; bail allowed. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1130; Muhammad Amjad Naeem v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 170-L/2025).
records.title: Muhammad Amjad Naeem v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 170-L/2025)

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.topic: S. 406 PPC: Loan Is Not Entrustment
records.text: Entrustment exists where property is temporarily handed over to be returned, creating a fiduciary relationship. A loan is not entrustment, because the lender expects return of equivalent value and not of the same property; the relationship is contractual. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1117; Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer (C.P.L.A. 1575/2024).
records.title: Ayesha Tayyab v. Station House Officer (C.P.L.A. 1575/2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Arbitration Award: Rule of Court though Application Time-Barred
records.text: Once an award is before the court, s. 17 Arbitration Act 1940 obliges it to examine the award and, if no objection succeeds, make it a rule of the court, even if a party's application for that purpose is time-barred. Limitation provisions restricting access to court are construed strictly. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 818, PLJ 2024 Lah 727.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Explains issues of fact, of law and mixed issues under O. XIV CPC. Where both arise, the court should decide all issues, but may try first an issue of law on jurisdiction or a statutory bar. Where an appellate court finds issues were not framed or tried, it may frame them and remit them for trial without remanding the whole case. Ref: 2025 CLC 323, PLJ 2024 Lah 253; Abdul Rahman v. Muhammad Farooq (R.F.A. 14953 of 2022).
records.title: Abdul Rahman v. Muhammad Farooq (R.F.A. 14953 of 2022)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: S. 12A Family Courts Act: Six-Month Disposal
records.text: S. 12A West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964 requires disposal within six months. The right to cross-examine does not extend to repeated adjournments; closure of cross-examination after numerous opportunities upheld. Interim orders are not open to challenge under s. 14(3) of the Act and may be questioned with the final decision. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 847; Khalid Pervaiz ul Haq v. Mst. Minha Asif (Civil Petition 930 of 2024).
records.title: Khalid Pervaiz ul Haq v. Mst. Minha Asif (Civil Petition 930 of 2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Arrest after Refusal of Pre-Arrest Bail
records.text: Once pre-arrest bail is refused, the accused is exposed to arrest. Police must not treat the mere filing of a petition before the Supreme Court as an implied stay; pendency of proceedings before a higher forum does not excuse failure to act in accordance with law. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 866; Zahid Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 645-L of 2025).
records.title: Zahid Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 645-L of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Standard of Proof for Defence Plea; Suppressed Injuries
records.text: The defence need only create a reasonable doubt, a lighter burden than the prosecution's. Suppression of injuries suffered by the accused showed the prosecution witnesses were not truthful. Ref: Iftikhar Ahmed alias Papu v. The State (Criminal Appeals 57 & 58 of 2021, decided 16.09.2025).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmed alias Papu v. The State (Criminal Appeals 57 & 58 of 2021, decided 16.09.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Eye-witnesses who could not prove why they were in another village at the time were chance witnesses. The witnesses attributed shots to the back of the deceased, but the doctor found those wounds to be exit wounds; this conflict showed the witnesses were not present. Ref: Iftikhar Ahmad alias Meena v. The State (Jail Petition 737 of 2017, decided 19.09.2025).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad alias Meena v. The State (Jail Petition 737 of 2017, decided 19.09.2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: Family pension is a daughter's right under the rules whether she is unmarried or divorced. A circular restricting it by marital status at the pensioner's death is contrary to the Act and Rules; circulars cannot override statute. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 856; Province of Sindh v. Mst. Sorath Fatima (C.P.L.A. 616-K/2025).
records.title: Province of Sindh v. Mst. Sorath Fatima (C.P.L.A. 616-K/2025)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.topic: DNA Test to Disprove Paternity Refused
records.text: Paternity of the minor having been settled by three courts in earlier litigation, a later ex parte decree could not unsettle it; refusal of DNA testing upheld. Muslim law strongly leans in favour of legitimacy. Ref: PLD 2025 SC 853; Muhammad Akhtar Hussain Pirzada v. Medical Superintendent, THQ Hospital Lodhran (C.P.L.A. 3984/2024).
records.title: Muhammad Akhtar Hussain Pirzada v. Medical Superintendent, THQ Hospital Lodhran (C.P.L.A. 3984/2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Physical and Judicial Remand: Ss. 167 and 344 CrPC
records.text: S. 167 CrPC allows a magistrate to remand an accused to police or judicial custody during investigation. S. 344 CrPC applies during inquiry or trial when proceedings are adjourned, and remand under it is only to judicial custody. Ref: PLD 2025 Lah 795.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: An FIR may be registered, and criminal proceedings initiated, through an attorney on behalf of the principal; with the court's permission the attorney may continue proceedings if the principal becomes unavailable. Ref: 2025 LHC 5989; Mirza Yahya Baig v. The State (Crl. Misc. 53550/25); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Mirza Yahya Baig v. The State (Crl. Misc. 53550/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 540 CrPC after Closure of Evidence; Confession
records.text: Closure of evidence brings certainty, but the court may still summon essential evidence under s. 540 CrPC to reach the truth. The judgment also explains the meaning, kinds and legal requirements of a confession, including that it must be voluntary and the accused warned that he is not bound to make it. Ref: Dr. Raheem Ullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 721-L/2025, decided 25.08.2025).
records.title: Dr. Raheem Ullah v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 721-L/2025, decided 25.08.2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Place of Occurrence; Delayed FIR; Witness Corroborating Himself
records.text: Without a report showing that earth taken from the spot was stained with human blood, the place of occurrence is not strictly proved. A recovery witness cannot corroborate his own ocular account. An FIR recorded later on a fresh application, after the complainant had narrated the occurrence to police at the spot, is not a true FIR under s. 154 CrPC. Motive is double-edged. Ref: 2025 MLD 1760, PLJ 2025 CrC 635; Ali Raza v. The State (Crl. A. 33146 & M.R. 155 of 2022).
records.title: Ali Raza v. The State (Crl. A. 33146 & M.R. 155 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Recovery of a sota from an open, public place (an empty plot next to the complainant's house) on the accused's disclosure was unsafe to rely on, particularly where it was not sent for testing for human blood. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1580; Muhammad Bilal v. The State (Criminal Appeal 172 of 2023).
records.title: Muhammad Bilal v. The State (Criminal Appeal 172 of 2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Appeal Not against Decree: O. XLI R. 1 CPC
records.text: An appeal not preferred against the decree was not competent. Although the decree was drawn during the appeal, the appellants never brought it on record or amended the appeal to challenge it, as O. XLI R. 1 CPC requires. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 987.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Bar of Jurisdiction: Mala Fide Acts (Canal Law)
records.text: Despite the bar of jurisdiction under the Canal and Drainage Act 1873 and the Punjab Irrigation, Drainage and Rivers Act 2023, the civil court may examine acts alleged in the plaint to be mala fide. The judgment also explains retrospective effect. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 968.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: A mother's remarriage does not by itself make her ineligible for custody of the minor. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 965.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC Dismissal Is on Merits: Res Judicata
records.text: Dismissal of a suit under O. XVII R. 3 CPC for failure to produce evidence is a decision on merits, so a later suit on the same matter is barred by s. 11 CPC. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 1003.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: The High Court will not exercise writ jurisdiction where the petitioner has an equally efficacious and adequate alternative remedy. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 1007.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Conditional Decree: Appeal Does Not Suspend Condition
records.text: An appeal by the decree-holder against a conditional decree for specific performance does not suspend the condition. He must still deposit the balance consideration where the decree itself states the consequence of non-compliance. Ref: PLJ 2025 Lah 1016.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.topic: Limitation for Appeal to Board of Revenue (s. 162 LRA)
records.text: S. 162 Land Revenue Act prescribes 90 days for an appeal against the Commissioner's order to the Board of Revenue, and s. 167 applies the Limitation Act 1908. Writ jurisdiction is discretionary and is exercised only for patent illegality causing failure of justice; petition dismissed. Ref: 2025 CLC 1217, PLJ 2025 Lah 1011; Muazzam Ali Goraya v. Member (Judicial-I) (WP 4078 of 2021).
records.title: Muazzam Ali Goraya v. Member (Judicial-I) (WP 4078 of 2021)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Statutory Delay after Direction to Conclude Trial
records.text: Where bail on statutory delay was earlier refused with a direction to conclude the trial, and the prosecution still fails to finish it after the statutory period under the third proviso to s. 497 CrPC, the accused becomes entitled to bail. Ref: Dawood v. The State (Cr.M (B.A) 639-M of 2025); Justice Sibghatullah.
records.title: Dawood v. The State (Cr.M (B.A) 639-M of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A CrPC: Registration Futile after Negative Inquiry
records.text: S. 154 CrPC ("shall") obliges the SHO to record an FIR, but s. 22-A CrPC ("may") gives the Justice of Peace discretion. Where a police inquiry under ss. 156, 157, 174 or 190 CrPC negates the occurrence, compelling registration under s. 22-A or s. 561-A CrPC is futile. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1320.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: An unusually short interval between occurrence, report and post-mortem cast doubt on whether all required steps could have been taken, suggesting the timings were manipulated. Appeal allowed; accused acquitted. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1391.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Semi-Open Eyes and Mouth of Deceased
records.text: Semi-open eyes and mouth of the deceased at post-mortem indicate the body lay unattended at the spot, casting doubt on the presence of the eye-witnesses. Ref: 2025 SCMR 1087, PLJ 2025 SC CrC 185.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: Any agreement, iqrarnama or compromise by which the mother waives her statutory right of hizanat (custody) of a minor is against law and cannot be enforced by a court. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 291.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A CDR shows only that a SIM was within the range of a cell tower, which covers a wide area, not who used the phone or where exactly. Without forensic analysis or recordings of the calls it is not conclusive of a witness's presence, and its production was rightly refused as not necessary for a just decision. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 1184.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Copy of CDR to Accused: Fair Trial
records.text: CDR collected by the investigating officer through a recovery memo but not appended to the report under s. 173 CrPC must be supplied to the accused, who cannot be surprised by evidence; due process under Art. 10-A of the Constitution requires it. Only the police diary under s. 172 CrPC is privileged. Ref: 2024 MLD 886.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 342 CrPC: Statement Read in Toto
records.text: Where the prosecution proves its case, the inculpatory part of the accused's statement under s. 342 CrPC may be read in support. Where the prosecution fails, the statement must be accepted or rejected as a whole. Ref: 2025 YLR 548.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Post-Arrest Bail: Accused Not Named in FIR
records.text: Murder case: petitioner not named in the FIR (two named accused and two unknown), later implicated as a hired assailant and brother of a named accused, on conflicting prosecution versions. Case of further inquiry under s. 497(2) CrPC; recovery and guilt left to trial. Bail granted. Ref: 2025 YLR 2696.

records.subject: Bail
records.text: The previous or subsequent conduct of an accused is relevant under Art. 21 QSO, including at the bail stage, to judge his intention and whether he is likely to repeat the offence. Ref: 2025 YLR 2172.

records.subject: Bail
records.text: CCTV footage, confirmed by the investigating officer, showed three accused arriving but only one carrying a firearm; the petitioner was unarmed, nothing was recovered from him and co-accused had been granted bail. Bail allowed. Ref: 2025 YLR 798.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: Safe City CCTV footage and stills relied on for identification were not proved: no expert certificate, no witness on how the video and photographs were made, contradictions about what was handed over, and the court merely marked the CD. Contents of a CD must be proved under the law of evidence and inspected by the court. Ref: 2025 YLR 1681.

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: CCTV Clips Free from Tampering: Bail
records.text: CCTV clips found by the Forensic Science Agency to be free from editing are admissible under Arts. 46-A and 164 QSO and may be considered at the bail stage. On the visuals, the complainant side appeared to be the aggressor; petitioner declared innocent by police and granted relief. Ref: 2024 YLR 762.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: In an unwitnessed murder where the culprit was traced through a neighbour's CCTV camera, the DVR could not be decoded and the forensic expert was not examined, so the footage had to be discarded. Ref: 2024 PCrLJ 1764.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV Not Sent to Forensic Laboratory
records.text: CCTV footage (CD and USB) taken from a bank manager was rightly discarded because the investigating officer never sent it to the Forensic Science Agency to verify authenticity; prosecution failed to prove its case. Ref: 2023 YLR 1691.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: CCTV: Contradictions on Recovery and Custody
records.text: Glaring contradictions between the shopkeeper witness and the investigating officer about how the CCTV recording was viewed and handed over made the recovery and safe custody of the CD doubtful. Ref: 2023 PCrLJ Note 8.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: A person who rescued an injured snow leopard cub, treated it and handed it to the Wildlife Conservator could not be proceeded against for its release costs or possession; no offence was made out and the proceedings were quashed as an abuse of process. Ref: 2025 PCrLJ 2044; Fahad Hanif v. Secretary Forest and Wildlife Gilgit-Baltistan.
records.title: Fahad Hanif v. Secretary Forest and Wildlife Gilgit-Baltistan

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Rejection of a plaint on the ground of res judicata, based on an earlier suit decided on compromise, was reversed. Except one respondent, the parties to the later suit were not parties to the earlier one, and the matter needed decision on evidence. Ref: PLD 2025 Pesh 59.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: S. 540-A CrPC allows the court to dispense with an accused's attendance where he is represented and there are several accused, or he cannot appear. The trial court was justified in acquitting such an accused in absentia where no prima facie case was made out and co-accused had been acquitted on the same evidence. Ref: 2025 YLR 2433.

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: Once declared hostile, a witness becomes a witness of none and his statement cannot be relied upon. Ref: 2025 YLR 2412.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Family Appeal: Restoration after Dismissal in Default
records.text: An appellate court hearing an appeal under s. 14 West Pakistan Family Courts Act 1964 may dismiss it for non-prosecution and may also restore it on sufficient cause. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 7; Ahmed Amin v. District Judge (WP 2787-19).
records.title: Ahmed Amin v. District Judge (WP 2787-19)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Cheque to Financial Institution: FIO, Not s. 489-F PPC
records.text: Where a cheque was issued to a financial institution for repayment of finance, the offence falls only under s. 20(4) Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance 2001 and s. 489-F PPC does not apply. Under s. 7 of the Ordinance the Banking Court has exclusive jurisdiction, and prosecution must be by complaint before it. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 69, 2026 CLD 303; Safeer Hussain v. CCPO Lahore (WP 48137/24).
records.title: Safeer Hussain v. CCPO Lahore (WP 48137/24)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: Prosecutors should call for the police record through WhatsApp one day before the case is fixed for hearing. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 7; Sunny Hakim v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33508/25); Justice Muhammad Amjad Rafiq.
records.title: Sunny Hakim v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33508/25)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Witnesses Unable to Give Ambulance Details
records.text: Eye-witnesses who said they took the deceased to hospital but could not give the vehicle number or the driver's name cast doubt on their own presence at the scene. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 105; Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 1096 of 2024).
records.title: Saeed Akhtar v. The State (Crl. Appeal 1096 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: Reviews the Constitution, CrPC, High Court Rules and Orders (Vol. III, Ch. 11-B) and Police Rules 1934 (Ch. 26, R. 20) on arrested persons. Under ss. 60 and 61 CrPC the arresting officer must produce the accused before a magistrate without unnecessary delay, and custody is then regulated under s. 167 CrPC; s. 58 CrPC alone allows pursuit and arrest anywhere in Pakistan. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 54; Irfan Ali v. Station House Officer (WP 10470/2025).
records.title: Irfan Ali v. Station House Officer (WP 10470/2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Restoration of Suit: Party in Jail
records.text: A plaintiff unable to pursue his suit while in jail showed sufficient cause; the trial court's discretionary order condoning delay and restoring the suit should not have been reversed in revision under s. 115 CPC. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2092; Ch. Fayyaz-ur-Rehman Khalid v. Amir Javed.
records.title: Ch. Fayyaz-ur-Rehman Khalid v. Amir Javed

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Children claiming that properties standing in their mother's name were benami must prove she was only an ostensible owner by cogent evidence, including the source of consideration; without such proof her title cannot be questioned. Ref: 2025 SCMR 2087; Mst. Nasira Ansari v. Tahira Begum (deceased).
records.title: Mst. Nasira Ansari v. Tahira Begum (deceased)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: If property entered as dower belongs to the husband's father or mother and they did not sign the nikahnama, they are not bound to transfer it as dower. Ref: PLD 2020 SC 269.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Timings Do Not Add Up; Delay in Post-mortem
records.text: The prosecution's timeline did not fit together: there was a delay of 7 hours 30 minutes in the post-mortem despite the short distance to the police station, and the motive was not established. These circumstances created reasonable doubt, the benefit of which went to the petitioner. Ref: 2026 SCMR 251; Ghulam Sarwar Ghangro v. The State (J.P. 166/2022).
records.title: Ghulam Sarwar Ghangro v. The State (J.P. 166/2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: A single injury jointly attributed to three accused, without saying who caused it, creates doubt about the appellant's involvement. Ref: 2026 SCMR 257; Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition 607/2020).
records.title: Laiq Shah v. The State (Crl. Petition 607/2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Additional Evidence (s. 428 CrPC) vs Remand (s. 423 CrPC)
records.text: S. 428 CrPC lets the appellate court record additional evidence where needed to avoid a miscarriage of justice, and then decide the appeal itself. Recording additional evidence under s. 428 and remanding a case to the trial court under s. 423 CrPC are distinct powers and must not be mixed. High Court directed to decide the jail appeal afresh. Ref: 2026 SCMR 308; Waseem Hassan Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 573/2025).
records.title: Waseem Hassan Khan v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 573/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: Christian citizens' right to seek dissolution or judicial separation in civil courts is part of their freedom to manage matters under their religious law. The courts below erred in not examining cruelty and admitted separation under ss. 10 and 22 of the Divorce Act, infringing Art. 10-A; guidance issued for such cases. Ref: 2026 LHC 1518; Shahroz v. ADJ (WP 2092-24, decided 23.02.2026); Justice Jawad Hassan.
records.title: Shahroz v. ADJ (WP 2092-24, decided 23.02.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: O. VII R. 13 CPC permits a fresh plaint after rejection, but does not excuse the plaintiff from disclosing the earlier litigation; non-disclosure was fatal to the later suit. Ref: 2026 LHC 1596; SNGPL v. Abdul Ghaffar (R.F.A. 69733/19, decided 11.03.2026); Justice Muzamil Akhtar Shabir.
records.title: SNGPL v. Abdul Ghaffar (R.F.A. 69733/19, decided 11.03.2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Government appeals filed late on the routine plea of inter-departmental procedures will not be condoned; every day's delay must be explained and the State is treated like any other litigant. The law helps the vigilant. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 113; Province of Sindh v. Abdul Tawab (C.A. 101-K/2022).
records.title: Province of Sindh v. Abdul Tawab (C.A. 101-K/2022)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 12(2) CPC by Non-Party; Lis Pendens
records.text: S. 12(2) CPC uses the word "person", so a non-party may apply to set aside a decree obtained by fraud or misrepresentation. A collusive or fraudulent compromise is not protected by s. 52 Transfer of Property Act 1882. Case remanded for framing issues and evidence. Ref: 2026 CLC 201; Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali (C.R. 4749 of 2015).
records.title: Bashir Ahmad v. Shaukat Ali (C.R. 4749 of 2015)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. VI R. 17 CPC: Late Amendment
records.text: Amendment of pleadings may be sought at any stage but is discretionary and allowed only if needed to decide the real controversy. An amendment sought after more than a decade, a full trial, decision and appeal was an afterthought to fill gaps and was refused. Ref: 2026 CLC 212.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: O. XVII R. 3 CPC: Failure to Produce Evidence
records.text: A plaintiff who failed for over 12 years after framing of issues to produce evidence, despite a final opportunity with warning and costs, was rightly non-suited under O. XVII R. 3 CPC. Ref: 2026 CLC 328.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Where the medico-legal report, post-mortem and site plan were prepared before the FIR was lodged, the principle that investigation follows the FIR was violated, a serious irregularity making the prosecution case doubtful (following Seeta Ram v. The State, 2025 SCMR 2028). Ref: Muhammad Usman v. The State (Jail Criminal Appeal 07/I of 2024, decided 10.03.2026).
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. The State (Jail Criminal Appeal 07/I of 2024, decided 10.03.2026)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Injuries prove a witness's presence but not his truthfulness; his evidence must still be tested by the usual standards. Delayed recording of witness statements and the maxim falsus in uno falsus in omnibus are also discussed. Ref: 2026 MLD 420, 2026 LHC 1911; Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl. Appeal 671-J of 2019).
records.title: Muhammad Zafar Iqbal v. The State (Crl. Appeal 671-J of 2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Limitation is a statute of repose and must be strictly applied; hardship, ignorance or poverty do not save it. A claim to inheritance must also cross limitation, waiver and acquiescence, and stale inheritance suits should not be encouraged. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 146; Jamshed Khan v. Akbar Khan (RSA 17025 of 2020).
records.title: Jamshed Khan v. Akbar Khan (RSA 17025 of 2020)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: The trial court allowed the prosecution to produce the deceased's widow, herself an accused, as a prosecution witness. A pardon under s. 337 CrPC requires the accused's free consent and a condition of full and true disclosure (with consequences under s. 339 CrPC); neither appeared on record, and under Art. 13 of the Constitution an accused cannot be compelled to testify against herself. Order set aside. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 372.

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Preliminary Inquiry before FIR; Delayed Post-mortem
records.text: Witnesses admitted that police recorded their statements before the FIR was registered, showing a preliminary inquiry that cast doubt on the content and timing of the FIR. Inordinate unexplained delay in the post-mortem, and eye-witnesses disbelieved against co-accused, added to the doubt. Appeal allowed and appellant acquitted; complainant's appeal against acquittal of co-accused dismissed in limine. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 362; Muhammad Riaz alias Baddi v. The State (Crl. Appeals 748-J & 870 of 2019; M.R. 46 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Riaz alias Baddi v. The State (Crl. Appeals 748-J & 870 of 2019; M.R. 46 of 2020)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Related but Natural Witnesses; Death Sentence Altered
records.text: Closely related eye-witnesses whose presence was natural (daylight, same locality, accused well known) were believed. Conviction under s. 302(b) PPC maintained, but sentence altered from death to imprisonment for life. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 201.

records.subject: Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)
records.text: The statement of an eight-year-old victim who told his mother within half an hour was spontaneous and reliable (res gestae, Art. 19 QSO). His identification of the accused at a properly held jail identification parade was substantive evidence. Conviction upheld; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 398; Asim Gulfraz v. The State (Jail Petition 390 of 2021).
records.title: Asim Gulfraz v. The State (Jail Petition 390 of 2021)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Abduction and Rape: 18-Day Delay; Unnamed Accused
records.text: FIR lodged 18 days late against unknown persons; the petitioner was not named and was implicated later. With the delay unexplained and the evidence doubtful, conviction set aside; petition converted into appeal and allowed, petitioner acquitted on benefit of doubt. Ref: 2026 SCMR 393; Maqsood Ali v. The State (Jail Petition 602 of 2019).
records.title: Maqsood Ali v. The State (Jail Petition 602 of 2019)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: CCTV footage was inconsequential where no site plan matched the camera's field of view to the place of occurrence and there was no proof of continuous recording, time synchronisation or safe custody. Accused acquitted; connected criminal petition dismissed as infructuous. Ref: 2026 SCMR 350; Fazal Mehmood v. The State (Jail Petition 217 of 2021; Criminal Petition 372 of 2022).
records.title: Fazal Mehmood v. The State (Jail Petition 217 of 2021; Criminal Petition 372 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Minor Variations in Ocular and Medical Evidence
records.text: Minor variations between the ocular and medical evidence about the seat of injuries are inconsequential; an eye-witness under attack cannot be expected to give a photographic account of each injury. Conviction upheld; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 317; Muhammad Ali v. The State (Jail Petition 541 of 2021).
records.title: Muhammad Ali v. The State (Jail Petition 541 of 2021)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Bridal Gifts Not Recoverable by Husband
records.text: The law distinguishes dower, dowry, bridal gifts and presents. Items given by the husband or his family in connection with the marriage are bridal gifts that vest absolutely in the bride and cannot be reclaimed by the husband. Ref: 2026 SCMR 561; Mst. Rafia Yaqoob v. Suleman Ayub (CP 2159 of 2025).
records.title: Mst. Rafia Yaqoob v. Suleman Ayub (CP 2159 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: The major penalty of dismissal from service cannot be imposed on a civil servant without a regular inquiry or an opportunity of hearing; doing so breaches natural justice. Ref: 2026 SCMR 576.

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: Pension is a constitutional and legal right, not charity, and cannot be refused for a late application or because the employee resigned after completing qualifying service (over 20 years). Federal Service Tribunal decision set aside. Ref: 2026 SCMR 429; Muhammad Usman v. Federation of Pakistan (C.P.L.A. 4065/2024); Justice Muhammad Shafi Siddiqui; Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan; Justice Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.
records.title: Muhammad Usman v. Federation of Pakistan (C.P.L.A. 4065/2024)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: In a night occurrence, the investigating officer never took the bulb, the claimed source of light, into possession. The failure to secure it created doubt; petition converted into appeal and allowed, appellants acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 434; Muhammad Waseem v. The State (Criminal Petition 406 of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Waseem v. The State (Criminal Petition 406 of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: Where a family court did not give adequate opportunity to file a written statement, another chance should be given. Speed must not lead to hurried decisions; justice delayed is denied, but justice hurried is buried. Ref: 2026 CLC 489; Muhammad Waqas v. Judge Family Court (WP 71055/25).
records.title: Muhammad Waqas v. Judge Family Court (WP 71055/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: The 2025 amendment to s. 43 PECA making offences under ss. 13 and 14 non-bailable is substantive, not procedural, and applies prospectively, because bail in a bailable offence is a vested right. Ref: 2026 MLD 542; Muhammad Rizwan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24).
records.title: Muhammad Rizwan v. The State (Crl. Misc. 10519-B-24)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.topic: Hostile Witness: Evidence Not Wholly Discarded
records.text: The evidence of a hostile witness is not wholly discarded; it is weighed with caution and the test is independent corroboration and consistency with the rest of the evidence. On the facts it was unsafe to base a capital conviction on it. Ref: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 264-J/2023; M.R. 21/2023).
records.title: Muhammad Asif v. The State (Crl. Appeal 264-J/2023; M.R. 21/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Where a common question of law has been decided in one case, another case on the same point that is time-barred may be heard on merits. Ref: 2026 MLD 507; Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ (WP 1829-24).
records.title: Benish Ghaffar v. ADJ (WP 1829-24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Party Impleaded at Appellate Stage: Remand
records.text: When a party is impleaded at the appellate stage under O. I R. 10 CPC, natural justice requires remand to the trial court so that the new party can plead, lead evidence and contest. Ref: 2026 YLR 536; Naeem Abbas v. Altaf Hussain (RFA 47-25).
records.title: Naeem Abbas v. Altaf Hussain (RFA 47-25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: CNIC Cannot Be Blocked by Civil Court
records.text: A CNIC is not the holder's movable property; it belongs to the Federal Government under s. 18 NADRA Ordinance 2000. Civil courts cannot attach, impound, cancel or block it as a coercive measure; only NADRA may act, on the grounds in s. 18. Ref: Muhammad Ali Ansari v. Federation of Pakistan (WP 8895 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Ali Ansari v. Federation of Pakistan (WP 8895 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Plaintiffs may not summon the defendant as their own witness to compel her into the box; this puts examination and cross-examination in the wrong hands and hinders a fair trial. Refusal upheld. Ref: PLD 2024 SC 976.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth: School Record
records.text: An entry in the school admission register, made when the plaintiff was ten, is reliable evidence of date of birth; the defendants did not dispute her documents. Concurrent findings set aside in revision and the suit for correction decreed. Ref: 2025 YLR 40.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.text: Recovery of 1005 grams of ice and 6000 grams of charas: contradictions in the witnesses' accounts of custody and transmission of the samples and case property broke the chain of custody. Conviction under ss. 9(d) and 11(c) of the 2019 Act set aside; petition converted into appeal and allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 937; Attique Ullah v. The State (Criminal Petition 1753).
records.title: Attique Ullah v. The State (Criminal Petition 1753)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Cross-firing between two groups in which a minor died; the minor's heirs compromised with the rival group, and a joint role was attributed to both sides. Who caused the fatal shot was a matter of further inquiry; post-arrest bail allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 914; Asad Khalil v. The State (Criminal Petition 868 of 2025).
records.title: Asad Khalil v. The State (Criminal Petition 868 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Oral Gift: Revocation and Title Documents
records.text: Dispute between a donee under an oral gift (1984), confirmed in writing and by mutation, and a later registered gift deed by the donor to his wife after revoking the oral gift. Possession of the original title documents was treated as decisive of ownership. Order of the single judge restored; appeal allowed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 929; Ghulam Asghar Khan v. Muhammad Arif Khan (Civil Appeal 8-K of 2020).
records.title: Ghulam Asghar Khan v. Muhammad Arif Khan (Civil Appeal 8-K of 2020)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Even where the offence falls within the prohibitory clause, bail cannot be refused on that ground alone; s. 337-N(2) PPC may be considered at the bail stage, and the gravity of the offence is no substitute for punishment. Post-arrest bail granted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 917; Muzamil Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition 974-L of 2025).
records.title: Muzamil Hussain v. The State (Criminal Petition 974-L of 2025)

records.subject: General Notes
records.topic: Supreme Court Judgments Not Binding on FCC
records.text: Under Art. 189 of the Constitution, Supreme Court judgments are not binding on the Federal Constitutional Court; they may be treated as persuasive. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 114; Muhammad Farhan v. Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. 16 of 2025).
records.title: Muhammad Farhan v. Province of Punjab (F.C.P.L.A. 16 of 2025)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt as of Right
records.text: Where there is doubt in the prosecution case, its benefit goes to the accused as of right. Ref: 2026 SCMR 891; Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition 473 of 2018).
records.title: Iftikhar alias Puppi v. The State (Jail Petition 473 of 2018)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Benefit of Doubt; Co-accused Acquitted; Negative Forensic Report
records.text: Even slight doubt benefits the accused. Witnesses attributed firing to five persons, three unknown in the FIR; co-accused were acquitted on the same evidence; the pistol recovered from the appellant did not match the empties. Appellant acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 921; Muhammad Amjad v. The State (Criminal Appeal 220-L of 2020).
records.title: Muhammad Amjad v. The State (Criminal Appeal 220-L of 2020)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Interfaith Marriage after Conversion: Custody Not Illegal
records.text: A father sought recovery of his daughter, claiming she was a minor Christian and her marriage void. Her declarations of conversion to Islam were sufficient and further probing into her faith was unwarranted; her marriage under the 1961 Ordinance stood, and her birth documents were not conclusive given her apparent age in court. Custody with her husband not illegal absent a court declaration otherwise; leave refused. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 138; Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. 536 of 2025).
records.title: Shahbaz Masih v. Additional Sessions Judge, Lahore (F.C.P.L.A. 536 of 2025)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: Where departmental proceedings rest on independent evidence of misconduct, acquittal in the criminal case does not end them. Where they rest only on the registration of an FIR, acquittal removes their basis and any penalty is unsustainable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 843, PLJ 2026 SC 118; Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat (C.P. 4757 of 2024).
records.title: Ghulam Murtaza v. District Police Officer, Gujrat (C.P. 4757 of 2024)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Blocking CNIC, Passport and Bank Accounts of Absent Witness
records.text: A trial court cannot order blocking of a complainant-witness's CNIC, passport or bank accounts for non-appearance: only NADRA may cancel or impound a CNIC (s. 18 NADRA Ordinance 2000), passports are governed by s. 8 Passports Act 1974, and NADRA cannot direct banks to block accounts. Order set aside; petitioner directed to appear. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 388; Abdul Rehman v. The State (Criminal Revision 205 of 2025).
records.title: Abdul Rehman v. The State (Criminal Revision 205 of 2025)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Document Not Produced: Reference in Cross-Examination
records.text: A document on which a claim is founded, if never produced in evidence, remains unproved; mere reference to it in cross-examination cannot replace strict proof. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 269, PLJ 2026 SC 322; Province of Punjab v. Zulfiqar (C.P.L.A. 1600-L of 2014).
records.title: Province of Punjab v. Zulfiqar (C.P.L.A. 1600-L of 2014)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Execution: CNIC of Judgment-Debtor Cannot Be Blocked
records.text: Section 51 CPC sets out the modes of executing a decree; the residuary clause (e) does not allow an executing court to block the judgment-debtor's CNIC. Doing so is not a proper exercise of discretion or statutory power, and the High Court erred in upholding it. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 280, PLJ 2026 SC 298; Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed (C.P.L.A. 3744/2023).
records.title: Agha Abid Majeed Khan v. Idrees Ahmed (C.P.L.A. 3744/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Correction of Date of Birth in Educational Record
records.text: Authority on correction of date of birth in educational record. Ref: 2020 SCMR 316.

records.subject: Passport Control List
records.text: A name cannot be placed on the Exit Control List merely because an FIR has been registered. Ref: 2026 MLD 250.

records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.text: Neither NCCIA nor FIA has authority to freeze the bank account of an accused. Ref: PLD 2026 Islamabad 63.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Civil Court Jurisdiction after Tenancy Ends
records.text: Civil courts may try all suits of a civil nature unless expressly or impliedly barred (s. 9 CPC). The Rent Tribunal has no jurisdiction over disputes arising after the tenancy ends, so the civil court is the proper forum for them. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 640; Fauzia Qayyum v. Additional District Judge (WP 55743/25).
records.title: Fauzia Qayyum v. Additional District Judge (WP 55743/25)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Recall of Ad-Interim Injunction: Not a Final Order
records.text: Recalling an ad-interim injunction because of repeated adjournment requests, to secure the petitioner's presence for arguments, regulates procedure and is not a final order; it is not ordinarily open to challenge unless perverse, illegal or without jurisdiction. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 610; Kaneez Begum v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 75498/25).
records.title: Kaneez Begum v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 75498/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.text: Traces the legislative history of the "book" prescribed under ss. 154 and 155 CrPC and sets out the course to follow where an FIR has been registered for a non-cognizable offence: preliminary investigation with the SP's direction, or a police report under s. 173 CrPC on which the magistrate may take cognizance under s. 190(1)(a) or (b). After preliminary investigation the accused may be arrested only on a warrant (s. 155(3) CrPC); on summons the magistrate may take a bond under s. 91 or commit to custody under s. 351 CrPC. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 663; Muhammad Ahsan v. The State (WP 25543/24).
records.title: Muhammad Ahsan v. The State (WP 25543/24)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: A gift made only to deprive other heirs out of malice may be invalid as zarar. But where the excluded children had distanced themselves and litigated against their father while the donee cared for him in old age, a gift of the whole estate to the donee is valid. Liaqat Ali v. Shahnaz Akhtar (2025 LHC 693) distinguished. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 630; Muhammad Naseem v. Asghar Ali Tabassum (Civil Revision 55105/23).
records.title: Muhammad Naseem v. Asghar Ali Tabassum (Civil Revision 55105/23)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: A third person's refusal to take a special oath is not a ground to dismiss a suit. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 627; Mst. Nasreen Akhtar v. ADJ (WP 724-20).
records.title: Mst. Nasreen Akhtar v. ADJ (WP 724-20)

records.subject: Qanun-e-Shahadat (QSO)
records.text: A document must be presented for registration within the prescribed time. A registered document carries strong evidentiary value and a presumption of correctness because it passes through verification. Ref: PLD 2026 FCC 304.
