records.subject: FIA & Anti-Corruption
records.topic: NAB Cases Transferred to Federal Constitutional Court
records.text: The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction in NAB cases under Art. 175F(a) of the Constitution read with ss. 32 and 32A NAO 1999. All pending NAB petitions and appeals stand transferred by fiction of law to the Federal Constitutional Court (judgment of 24 July 2026). Ref: PLD 2026 SC 424; Chairman NAB v. Adeel Ahmed (Crl.P.L.A. 316/2018).
records.title: Chairman NAB v. Adeel Ahmed (Crl.P.L.A. 316/2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Limitation under the Supreme Court Rules 2025 is substantive. The State must meet the time limits and cannot rely on internal file movement, committee schedules or staff shortages as sufficient cause. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 376; Federation of Pakistan v. Farid Ullah (C.P.L.A. 4430/2025).
records.title: Federation of Pakistan v. Farid Ullah (C.P.L.A. 4430/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: Where property is entered in the nikahnama as dower payable on demand, the husband must keep it available for transfer whenever the wife demands it. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 371; Sajid Hussain v. Additional District Judge, Vehari (CPLA 1330-L of 2025).
records.title: Sajid Hussain v. Additional District Judge, Vehari (CPLA 1330-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Conversion to Islam: Marriage to Non-Muslim Husband
records.text: Considers the legal and Shariah status of the marriage of a non-Muslim woman to her non-Muslim husband after her conversion to Islam. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 617; Noor Fatima v. Station House Officer (WP 622/2025).
records.title: Noor Fatima v. Station House Officer (WP 622/2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: A wife is entitled to dissolution of marriage if the husband contracts a second marriage in breach of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961. Ref: PLD 2026 SC 302, PLD 2026 SC 91, PLD 2025 SC 262.

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 94 CrPC: Geo-Fencing and CDR of Witnesses
records.text: Under s. 94 CrPC an accused may seek production of any document, including geo-fencing data and CDR of prosecution witnesses, at any stage to test their claimed presence, if the court finds it necessary or desirable. The discretion must be exercised judiciously to reach a just decision. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1334.

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Road Certificate: Documentary Proof of Dispatch
records.text: An entry in the road certificate about dispatch of case property can be negated only by a document of superior value, not by oral evidence. Where the investigating officer and the moharrar gave conflicting accounts of who took the sample parcel to the PFSA, safe transmission was not proved. Road certificates must record the required details expressly. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1639, PLJ 2026 CrC 669; Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 68455/23).
records.title: Naseem alias Seemay Shah v. The State (Crl. A. 68455/23)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Dowry Dispute Not Criminal Breach of Trust
records.text: A dispute between spouses over dowry articles is for the Family Court and cannot be turned into an offence under s. 406 PPC merely by calling the articles "amanat". Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 678; Muhammad Umair Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 9787/26).
records.title: Muhammad Umair Riaz v. The State (Crl. Misc. 9787/26)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Infirmity a Separate Ground for Bail
records.text: S. 497 CrPC recognises "infirmity" as a ground for bail separate from sickness, even in heinous offences. Infirmity covers frailty from age, congenital limitation or non-fatal disease restricting mobility. If the court itself finds the prisoner infirm it may grant bail without further medical inquiry. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 707; Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33164/26).
records.title: Iftikhar Ahmad v. The State (Crl. Misc. 33164/26)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 22-A CrPC: Transfer between Justices of Peace
records.text: A Sessions Judge acting administratively may entrust an application under s. 22-A(6) CrPC to an Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace, but cannot later transfer it to another Ex-Officio Justice of the Peace. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 581; Faisal Manzoor v. District & Sessions Judge (WP 41376/26).
records.title: Faisal Manzoor v. District & Sessions Judge (WP 41376/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: The forum of appeal against a grant or refusal of a succession certificate is governed by ss. 384 and 388 Succession Act 1925, not pecuniary limits. An appeal from a Civil Judge with delegated powers under s. 388 lies to the District Judge whatever the value of the estate; returning it was a jurisdictional error. Appeal restored. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 606; Sheikh Imam Baksh v. Mst. Gulzar Begum (Civil Revision 35921/25).
records.title: Sheikh Imam Baksh v. Mst. Gulzar Begum (Civil Revision 35921/25)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Doubtful medical evidence of a finger fracture with no injury to the rest of the hand suggested a friendly-hand injury, making out a case for pre-arrest bail. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 658; Umar Farooq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 15322/26).
records.title: Umar Farooq v. The State (Crl. Misc. 15322/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Arrest of Judgment-Debtor: S. 51 and O. XXI R. 40 CPC
records.text: Arrest and detention of a judgment-debtor in execution of a money decree is an exceptional mode, available only on strict compliance with the safeguards in s. 51 and O. XXI R. 40 CPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 642; Naseer Ahmad Nasir v. Ali Sher (WP 31402/26); Justice Ahmad Nadeem Arshad.
records.title: Naseer Ahmad Nasir v. Ali Sher (WP 31402/26)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Referral of Public Functionary for Departmental Action
records.text: Where a public functionary appears to obstruct execution of judicial orders, the court may refer the matter to the competent authority for departmental action. Such a referral is recommendatory, makes no finding of guilt, and is not ordinarily interfered with in writ jurisdiction. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 658; Muhammad Sufyan v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 12495/26).
records.title: Muhammad Sufyan v. Additional District Judge (Misc. Writ 12495/26)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.text: An oral extension of tenancy, unless the other side concedes it, operates at most for one month; a claimed oral extension of 15 years could not be assumed. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 663; Khizar Hayyat v. ADJ (WP 7652-26).
records.title: Khizar Hayyat v. ADJ (WP 7652-26)

records.subject: General Notes
records.text: A licence for a Muharram procession or majlis is needed only where the police judge it to threaten the peace; restrictions on such assemblies are otherwise unjustified. Ref: PLJ 2026 Lah 668; Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO (WP 7251-26).
records.title: Syed Wasi Haider v. CPO (WP 7251-26)

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: In fixing a minor's maintenance the court considers the child's reasonable needs and the father's means, income and status. Higher courts interfere with the amount only if it is arbitrary, unreasonable or contrary to law. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 518; Mst. Shaheen Nawaz v. Raheel Khan (C.P.L.A. 316-K/2026).
records.title: Mst. Shaheen Nawaz v. Raheel Khan (C.P.L.A. 316-K/2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Under O. III R. 4 CPC and s. 22(3) Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act 1973, a wakalatnama does not give unlimited authority to compromise or withdraw. But a statement or concession made in open court by duly engaged counsel cannot be disowned as a matter of convenience without proof of lack of authority or fraud; a party cannot approbate and reprobate. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC 521; Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali (C.P.L.A. 49-K/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Ashraf v. Akber Ali (C.P.L.A. 49-K/2026)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Rent Proceedings: Delay and Dilatory Tactics
records.text: Rent laws are a special summary code for speedy decision. Courts must not let rent cases drag through repeated applications, revisions and appeals for decades; statutory timelines must be followed and mala fide adjournments and applications discouraged. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1995, PLJ 2026 SC 546; Muhammad Jahangir v. Haji Muhammad Ashraf (C.A. 2555/2016).
records.title: Muhammad Jahangir v. Haji Muhammad Ashraf (C.A. 2555/2016)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Prompt lodging of the FIR secures the earliest account of the time, culprits, roles, weapons and witnesses. Delay often leads to embellishment as an afterthought. Ref: PLJ 2026 CrC 740; Musharaf Habib v. The State (Crl. Appeal 821 of 2017).
records.title: Musharaf Habib v. The State (Crl. Appeal 821 of 2017)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: Land acquisition for a public purpose is governed by the self-contained regime of the Land Acquisition Act 1894; parties must seek relief under that Act. Ref: PLJ 2026 FCC 111; C.P.L.A. 3912 of 2025, C.P.L.A. 1449 of 2025 and C.M.A. 1142-L of 2025.
records.title: C.P.L.A. 3912 of 2025, C.P.L.A. 1449 of 2025 and C.M.A. 1142-L of 2025

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.text: Narcotics enforcement mostly reaches street-level peddlers, not the principal traffickers. The seriousness of the offence does not lower the standard of proof; because punishments are harsh, courts must insist on strict proof of recovery, custody, sampling, transmission and conscious possession. Judgment circulated to IGPs, Prosecutors General and DPOs. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 273; Mehmood Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 1544 of 2025).
records.title: Mehmood Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 1544 of 2025)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Punjab Food Authority: Release of Seized Items
records.text: The Punjab Food Authority Act 2011 sets up three regimes: the Food Safety Officer, the Food Authority and the Special Court, each with distinct powers (ss. 7, 12, 13 and 39). Seized food or premises may be released during proceedings against a surety bond, without prejudice to the final decision, as with case property under the CrPC. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 744; Abdul Qadeer v. The State (WP 10163 of 2026).
records.title: Abdul Qadeer v. The State (WP 10163 of 2026)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: S. 26-A CPC: Penal Action for Late Written Statement
records.text: S. 26-A CPC aims to shorten litigation, but before penal consequences are imposed the defendant's conduct must be examined; where he acted in good faith or was prevented by genuine circumstances from filing the written statement in time, strict penal action may not be warranted. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 734.

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Summary Suit: Death of Drawer; Execution against Heirs
records.text: A summary suit under O. XXXVII CPC validly filed against the drawer in his lifetime does not fail on his death where his legal representatives were impleaded, adopted his written statement and contested on merits; they cannot raise maintainability under ss. 29 and 29-A Negotiable Instruments Act for the first time in appeal. Under s. 50 CPC the decree is executable against them only to the extent of the estate inherited. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 716, PLJ 2026 Lah 534.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: When fixing maintenance for minors, the court takes an inquisitorial role. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 767, PLJ 2026 Lah 260; Muhammad Saeed Anwar v. Judge Family Court (WP 26445/22).
records.title: Muhammad Saeed Anwar v. Judge Family Court (WP 26445/22)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: No Change of Investigation after Charge
records.text: Investigation cannot be changed after the charge has been framed. Ref: 2026 PCrLJ 1759; Maryam Bibi v. The State (WP 45328/25).
records.title: Maryam Bibi v. The State (WP 45328/25)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: Delay in Registration of FIR: Duty of Police
records.text: The FIR is not substantive evidence, but delay in registering it gives room for false implication and manipulation of evidence. Prompt registration lets the police secure the scene and evidence; the Court stressed police accountability for proper investigation. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1409; Mir Muhammad alias Kurary v. The State (Criminal Appeal 40-K of 2022).
records.title: Mir Muhammad alias Kurary v. The State (Criminal Appeal 40-K of 2022)

records.subject: Bail
records.topic: Gravity of Offence No Bar Where Further Inquiry
records.text: The gravity or atrocity of an offence alone does not justify refusing bail, pre-arrest or post-arrest, where the evidence leaves the case one of further inquiry; bail cannot be withheld as punishment. Like cases should be treated alike, after assessing each accused's role. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1422; Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025).
records.title: Kashif Tanveer v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 562-L of 2025)

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Annual Increase in Maintenance: Not Compounded
records.text: Where a maintenance decree is silent on compounding, the annual increase (here 20%) is calculated on the originally decreed amount, not on the enhanced amount of the previous year. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1582, PLJ 2026 SC 429; Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid (C.P.L.A. 3204 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Waqar Wasi v. Mst. Amber Abid (C.P.L.A. 3204 of 2022)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: Documentary proof of age is preferred over an ossification test in an inquiry under s. 8 Juvenile Justice System Act 2018, and the trial court has ample power to hold that inquiry. Ref: 2026 LHC 5998; Ali Shair alias Malhi v. Additional Sessions Judge (Crl. Revision 49478/26, decided 17.09.2026); Justice Amir Ajam Malik.
records.title: Ali Shair alias Malhi v. Additional Sessions Judge (Crl. Revision 49478/26, decided 17.09.2026)

records.subject: DNA Test
records.text: Collecting a person's DNA without due process violates privacy, dignity and liberty under Art. 9 of the Constitution, given the sensitivity of genetic information. An arbitrary demand for DNA in an anti-corruption case was not sustainable. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1780; Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti-Corruption, Pakpattan (Crl.P.L.A. 106/2023).
records.title: Khalid Hameed v. Special Judge Anti-Corruption, Pakpattan (Crl.P.L.A. 106/2023)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.text: A judicial confession setting out exact dates, times and places of many murders in a structured way looked prepared rather than spontaneous, raising serious doubt about its voluntariness and truth; it could not safely sustain a capital conviction. The judgment also covers the value of a retracted confession and the fair trial guarantee in Art. 10-A. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 308; Ahmed Saeed alias Bharam alias Nagori v. The State (Criminal Appeal 649/2022 in J.P. 385/2019).
records.title: Ahmed Saeed alias Bharam alias Nagori v. The State (Criminal Appeal 649/2022 in J.P. 385/2019)

records.subject: Criminal Trial / Murder
records.topic: Grave and Sudden Provocation: S. 302(c) PPC
records.text: Where the accused lost self-control and the occurrence happened on the spur of the moment, the case fell within s. 302(c) PPC. Ref: PLJ 2026 SC CrC 316; Muhammad Nasir Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition 459 of 2022).
records.title: Muhammad Nasir Hussain v. The State (Jail Petition 459 of 2022)

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.topic: Minor Victim; Negative DNA; Potency Test
records.text: The identity of rape victims must be protected. The testimony of a minor victim can by itself sustain a conviction. A negative DNA report is only corroborative, and a potency test shows capacity, not commission. Ref: 2026 MLD 1618.

records.subject: Family Law
records.topic: Counsel Cannot Tender Documents in Evidence
records.text: Counsel may file and present documents under O. XIII CPC, but documents must be proved through witnesses; counsel cannot tender them in evidence through his own statement, including in family cases. A decree does not bind on paternity a person who was not a party. Ref: 2026 MLD 1693; Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge (WP 71795/2023).
records.title: Naeem Niaz Awan v. Additional District Judge (WP 71795/2023)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: A decree-holder must file the first execution petition within three years under Art. 181 Limitation Act 1908. If he fails, the right to execute is lost and cannot be revived by a later petition under s. 48 CPC. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1785, PLJ 2026 SC 580; Rasheed (deceased) v. Muhammad Azam Khan (Civil Petition 4530 of 2024).
records.title: Rasheed (deceased) v. Muhammad Azam Khan (Civil Petition 4530 of 2024)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.text: A person who builds on or improves another's property without the owner's consent, such as a tenant or permissive occupant, does so at his own risk and gains no title or right to compensation. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1967, PLJ 2026 SC 478; Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal 140-P of 2018).
records.title: Sher Said v. Umar Akhtar (Civil Appeal 140-P of 2018)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: Registered Power of Attorney: Authority to Sell
records.text: A registered power of attorney is presumed duly executed under Art. 95 QSO. Authority to sell includes authority to enter into an antecedent agreement to sell. The High Court erred in revision by reversing concurrent findings on a restrictive reading of the power; appeals allowed and trial and appellate decrees for specific performance restored. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1978; Saad Younis v. Ghulam Bari (C.A. 435-L/2012).
records.title: Saad Younis v. Ghulam Bari (C.A. 435-L/2012)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.topic: Co-owner Eviction; Bona Fide Need of Family
records.text: One co-owner can seek eviction on behalf of all. Bona fide personal need extends to the landlord's co-sharers, children and family, and the landlord may choose which premises suit him. Eviction orders upheld; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1825; Najeeb Ullah v. Syed Shams-ud-Din (Civil Petitions 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025).
records.title: Najeeb Ullah v. Syed Shams-ud-Din (Civil Petitions 300-Q, 303-Q to 312-Q of 2025)

records.subject: Rent Matters
records.text: The landlord is the sole judge of his requirement and choice of premises. His sworn testimony alone can prove bona fide personal need if consistent with the ejectment application. High Court's order set aside for misreading evidence; eviction restored, tenant given six months to vacate. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1931; Nafees Ahmed v. Mst. Shaheen Begum.
records.title: Nafees Ahmed v. Mst. Shaheen Begum

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.text: Larger bench (five judges): the requirement to state "full protocols" in a chemical examiner's report under unamended rule 6 of the 2001 Rules is directory; non-compliance does not by itself invalidate the report under s. 36(2) CNSA. Under amended rule 6, naming the recognised tests listed in its Explanation is sufficient compliance. No retrospective effect. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1862, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 337; Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A. 43/2020).
records.title: Baz Khan v. The State (Crl.A. 43/2020)

records.subject: Service Matters
records.text: In contempt proceedings over non-implementation of an order to appoint the petitioner as Sub-Inspector in the Punjab Police, the department's conditional and delayed steps were not genuine compliance. The department was warned to implement within 30 days, with liberty to the petitioner to pursue contempt if it did not. Ref: PLD 2026 Lah 771.

records.subject: Board of Revenue
records.text: A suit to restore 1956-57 revenue entries and undo later mutations, after third-party rights had arisen, raised limitation and the civil court bar in s. 172 West Pakistan Land Revenue Act 1967. The courts below reappraised evidence without deciding maintainability; petition converted into appeal and allowed, suit dismissed, respondents left to the revenue hierarchy. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1817, PLJ 2026 SC 415; Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. 1086/2019).
records.title: Nadeem Akhtar (deceased) v. Manzoor Ahmad (C.P.L.A. 1086/2019)

records.subject: Civil Procedure (CPC) & Civil Law
records.topic: New Plea before Supreme Court; Unproved Document
records.text: A party cannot set up a new case for the first time before the Supreme Court, and evidence beyond pleadings is of no effect. An unproved panchayat nama could not defeat title shown in a sanctioned mutation; a scribe's evidence cannot replace proof through attesting witnesses. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1905, PLJ 2026 SC 443; Anwar Ali Shah v. Sadiq Ali Shah (C.A. 1410 of 2019).
records.title: Anwar Ali Shah v. Sadiq Ali Shah (C.A. 1410 of 2019)

records.subject: Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)
records.topic: S. 360 CrPC: Correcting Evidence Recorded by Video Link
records.text: S. 360(1) CrPC requires a completed deposition to be read over and corrected; s. 360(2) lets a witness object and requires a memorandum with the correct version. Where a witness disputes the written record of her video-link evidence, the trial court must compare it with the recording and record any correction. Orders refusing this set aside (Art. 10-A). Ref: PLD 2026 SC 498, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 283; Mst. Nayab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1033/2024).
records.title: Mst. Nayab v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 1033/2024)

records.subject: Bail
records.text: The third proviso to s. 497(1) CrPC gives a substantive right to bail if trial is not concluded in time. Only a visible and concerted effort by the accused to delay the trial defeats it; ordinary adjournments or isolated requests do not. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1834; Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 449-L/2026).
records.title: Muhammad Iqbal v. The State (Crl.P.L.A. 449-L/2026)

records.subject: CNSA: Bail & Trial
records.topic: Conscious Possession; Custody of Case Property
records.text: 27 kg of charas allegedly found in secret cavities of a vehicle: the vehicle and cavities were not produced, ownership was not proved through excise records, the investigating officer and moharrir contradicted each other on who handed over the case property, and no malkhana register or road certificate was produced. Conscious possession and safe custody not proved; acquitted. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1830, PLJ 2026 SC CrC 279; Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 51 of 2023).
records.title: Alam Khan v. The State (Criminal Petition 51 of 2023)

records.subject: Character Certificate
records.topic: Minor Conviction on Plea of Guilt
records.text: The petitioner was convicted on his own plea of guilt under the Ehtram-e-Ramazan Ordinance 1981 and fined Rs. 1,000. Showing that minor conviction in his police clearance certificate for all time stigmatised him; respondents directed to issue the certificate accordingly. Ref: PLD 2026 Pesh 226.

records.subject: Family Law
records.text: Gold ornaments gifted to the bride by her parents for her exclusive use are her personal property; their retention by the husband or his family can be remedied through the Family Court. Reduction of the decree from 87 to 44 tolas left undisturbed; leave refused. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1838.

records.subject: Rape (s. 376 PPC)
records.text: The testimony of a child victim with a firm core on identity, place, force and threat can sustain a conviction; a restrained narration does not weaken it. On sentence, the court held that proof of guilt does not settle the choice between death and life imprisonment; conviction maintained, death sentence converted to imprisonment for life. Directions issued to protect child victims. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1842.

records.subject: Bail
records.text: Grant and cancellation of bail follow different principles. Bail is cancelled under s. 497(5) CrPC only if granted in breach of law or settled principles, or if the accused misuses it (tampering, intimidating witnesses). The Supreme Court does not interfere with a High Court's bail order unless the discretion is fanciful or arbitrary; petition for cancellation dismissed. Ref: 2026 SCMR 1963.
